items.front: In Aurora, when the writer fails and the cluster has an Aurora Replica, service is typically restored in {{c1::less than 60 seconds}}.
items.extra: Often in [less than 30 seconds](../facts/aurora.md#aurora-failover-time-with-replica-guide).

items.front: In Aurora, when the writer fails and the cluster has no Aurora Replica, service typically returns in {{c1::less than 10 minutes}}.
items.extra: With no Aurora Replica to promote, Aurora creates a new primary instance.

items.front: In Aurora, the lag of an Aurora Replica behind the writer is usually {{c1::much less than 100 milliseconds}}.
items.extra: Replica lag varies with the rate of database change.

items.front: In Aurora Global Database, replication to the secondary Regions has a latency of {{c1::typically under a second}}.
items.extra: Aurora replicates over dedicated infrastructure, so the primary stays fully available.

items.front: Aurora Replica or RDS read replica: which one shares the storage volume of the primary instance?
items.back: The Aurora Replica.
items.extra: Aurora Replicas [connect to the same storage volume](../facts/aurora.md#aurora-adding-replicas-read-same-volume-offload) as the primary DB instance.

items.front: In Aurora, cluster endpoint or reader endpoint: which one accepts writes?
items.back: The cluster endpoint.
items.extra: The cluster endpoint is [the only one that can perform write operations](../facts/aurora.md#aurora-cluster-endpoint-only-one-for-writes).

items.front: In Aurora, a new database has spiky load that is hard to predict. Which capacity option fits?
items.back: Aurora Serverless v2. It scales inside a capacity range you set.
items.extra: AWS says Aurora serverless is intended for [variable or "spiky" workloads](../facts/aurora-serverless.md#aurora-serverless-choose-variable-spiky-workloads).

items.front: In Aurora, a relational database must recover in another Region with a recovery point objective (RPO) of seconds. What do you use?
items.back: Aurora Global Database.
items.extra: For an Aurora global database, RPO is [typically measured in seconds](../facts/aurora.md#aurora-global-rpo-typically-seconds-guide).

items.front: In an Aurora global database, can a secondary cluster accept writes on its own?
items.back: No. Only the primary cluster performs write operations.
items.extra: With write forwarding turned on, a secondary cluster can [forward SQL statements that perform write operations](../facts/aurora.md#aurora-write-forwarding-secondary-forward-sql-writes) to the primary cluster.

items.front: In Aurora, can you turn on encryption for an existing unencrypted DB cluster?
items.back: No. Restore a snapshot to a new encrypted cluster.
items.extra: You [can't convert an unencrypted DB cluster](../facts/aurora.md#aurora-encryption-cannot-convert-unencrypted-in-place) to an encrypted one. You can [restore an unencrypted snapshot](../facts/aurora.md#aurora-encryption-cannot-convert-unencrypted-in-place) to an encrypted cluster with a KMS key.

items.front: In Aurora Global Database, failover or switchover: which one recovers from a Region outage?
items.back: Failover. Switchover is for healthy clusters.
items.extra: Switchovers are designed for clusters [in a healthy state](../facts/aurora.md#aurora-global-db-switchover-healthy-only-unplanned-use-failover).

items.front: In Aurora Global Database, is a failover after a Region outage free of data loss?
items.back: No. Writes not yet replicated to the secondary can be lost.
items.extra: The promoted cluster is still in a transactionally consistent state.

items.front: In Aurora, can Aurora Auto Scaling add capacity for the writer instance?
items.back: No. It helps with the reader instances only.
items.extra: Aurora Auto Scaling helps with the workload [only on the reader instances](../facts/aurora.md#aurora-autoscaling-writer-not-scaled).

items.front: In Aurora, does the reader endpoint balance each individual query?
items.back: No. It balances connections, not individual queries.
items.extra: The reader endpoint [balances connections to available Aurora Replicas](../facts/aurora.md#aurora-reader-endpoint-balances-connections-not-queries).

items.front: In Aurora Serverless v2, does an idle instance pause when the minimum capacity is above zero ACUs?
items.back: No. Auto-pause needs a minimum capacity of zero ACUs.
items.extra: With a minimum [higher than zero ACUs](../facts/aurora-serverless.md#aurora-serverless-min-capacity-above-zero-no-pause), the instances do not pause.

items.front: In Aurora PostgreSQL, can a DB cluster have a cross-Region Aurora Replica?
items.back: No. Use Aurora Global Database for other Regions.
items.extra: Aurora PostgreSQL [doesn't support cross-Region Aurora Replicas](../facts/aurora.md#aurora-postgres-no-cross-region-aurora-replicas).

items.front: In Aurora, does a point-in-time restore roll back the running DB cluster?
items.back: No. It creates a new DB cluster.
items.extra: A restore to a point in time ends by [creating a new DB cluster](../facts/aurora.md#aurora-pitr-creates-new-cluster).

items.front: In Aurora, a new database will grow to a size nobody can predict. How much storage do you allocate in advance?
items.back: None. The cluster volume grows as the data grows.
items.extra: You do not [provision either storage or I/O operations in advance](../facts/aurora.md#aurora-pricing-storage-io-not-provisioned-in-advance), and you are [only charged for the space that you use](../facts/aurora.md#aurora-charged-only-for-space-used).

items.front: In Aurora, reporting queries must run on the largest Aurora Replicas and nowhere else. What do the reports connect to?
items.back: A custom endpoint that groups those replicas.
items.extra: A custom endpoint represents [a set of DB instances that you choose](../facts/aurora.md#aurora-custom-endpoint-set-of-chosen-instances).

items.front: In Aurora, a team needs a quick test copy of production data. What do you use?
items.back: An Aurora clone. It adds storage only for changed data.
items.extra: Additional storage is [allocated only when changes are made to data](../facts/aurora.md#aurora-clone-copy-on-write-storage-on-change).

items.front: Moving an Oracle database to Aurora PostgreSQL: which AWS tool converts the database schema?
items.back: AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT).
items.extra: AWS suggests it when the source has a [different underlying engine than Aurora's](../facts/aurora.md#aurora-migrate-heterogeneous-consider-sct).

items.front: In Aurora, you move RDS for PostgreSQL to Aurora PostgreSQL with a short cutover. Which path fits?
items.back: An Aurora read replica, promoted when replica lag is zero.
items.extra: AWS uses this approach for [migration to Aurora PostgreSQL](../facts/aurora.md#aurora-rds-postgres-read-replica-for-migration), not for ongoing replication.

items.front: Aurora Global Database or DynamoDB global tables: which one accepts writes in every Region?
items.back: DynamoDB global tables.
items.extra: [Any global table replica](../facts/dynamodb.md#dynamodb-global-table-any-replica-serves-reads-writes) can serve reads and writes. In Aurora Global Database, the [primary cluster](../facts/aurora.md#aurora-global-db-only-primary-writes) performs the writes.

items.front: In Aurora, does a new DB instance in the cluster get its own copy of the data?
items.back: No. It connects to the shared cluster volume.
items.extra: Aurora [doesn't make a new copy](../facts/aurora.md#aurora-add-instance-no-data-copy) of the table data.

items.front: In Aurora, a restorable copy of a database must be kept for many years. What do you use?
items.back: A manual DB cluster snapshot. Snapshots do not expire.
items.extra: Aurora DB cluster [snapshots don't expire](../facts/aurora.md#aurora-snapshots-do-not-expire).

items.front: In Aurora, each DB cluster can have {{c1::up to 15 Aurora Replicas in addition to the primary DB instance}}.
items.extra: The Aurora Replicas serve reads, and the primary DB instance serves writes.

items.front: In Aurora, the cluster volume of each DB cluster keeps {{c1::six copies}} of all your data, spread across three AZs.
items.extra: Aurora replicates the data, but [you only pay for one copy](../facts/aurora.md#aurora-faq-pay-for-one-copy).

items.front: In Aurora Global Database, AWS says a secondary Region can be promoted to read and write in {{c1::less than 1 minute}}.
items.extra: The user guide says the recovery time objective (RTO) can be [in the order of minutes](../facts/aurora.md#aurora-global-rto-order-of-minutes-guide).

items.front: In Aurora, you can set a backup retention period of {{c1::1–35 days}}.
items.extra: The default retention period is [one day](../facts/aurora.md#aurora-backup-retention-default-1-day).

items.front: In Aurora, I/O charges are a large share of the database bill. Which storage configuration fits?
items.back: Aurora I/O-Optimized. It is best at 25% or more of spend.
items.extra: With I/O-Optimized there are [no additional charges for read and write I/O](../facts/aurora.md#aurora-io-optimized-no-io-charges).

items.front: In Aurora PostgreSQL, can you backtrack a DB cluster to an earlier time?
items.back: No. Backtrack is an Aurora MySQL feature.
items.extra: [Backtrack is not available for Aurora PostgreSQL](../facts/aurora.md#aurora-backtrack-not-for-postgresql). A point-in-time restore works by [creating a new DB cluster](../facts/aurora.md#aurora-pitr-creates-new-cluster).

items.front: In Aurora Serverless v2, a development database is idle most of the week. How do you stop paying for its compute?
items.back: Set the minimum capacity to zero ACUs, so it can pause.
items.extra: While an instance is auto-paused, its [instance charge is zero](../facts/aurora-serverless.md#aurora-serverless-auto-pause-billing-storage-still-charged). Storage is still charged.
